All six works are general software-engineering mutation-testing methodology; none addresses neuron models, stimulation protocols or electrophysiology. They are background for NeuroSem's mutant classification, redundancy handling and size-matched baselines, not anticipations of the integrated method.

rows.citation: Madeyski L, Orzeszyna W, Torkar R, et al. (2014). Overcoming the Equivalent Mutant Problem: A Systematic Literature Review and a Comparative Experiment of Second Order Mutation. IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 40(1):23-42.
rows.model_type: general software (Java programs under mutation testing); systematic literature review plus controlled experiment
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - compares first-order mutation with four second-order mutation strategies, measuring how many generated mutants are equivalent.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - software test suites kill mutants; no stimulation protocols or dynamical-system inputs.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no electrophysiology; outcomes are mutant counts, kill status, runtime and manual classification effort.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - compares mutation-generation strategies; no selection or minimisation of a test or protocol battery reported in the abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - abstract reports no discovery/held-out split of programs or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-assisted code transformations.
rows.software: none (abstract names a JudyDiffOp strategy; no tool URL retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Provides the detect/suggest/avoid taxonomy for equivalent mutants. NeuroSem instead labels behavioural equivalence empirically for NeuroML neuron models via an exhaustive stimulation battery with refinement-calibrated tolerances, without claiming proof of equivalence.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1109/tse.2013.44 (title, 4 authors, TSE 40(1) 23-42, 2014-01); OpenAlex W2097599402 abstract.

rows.citation: Papadakis M, Jia Y, Harman M, et al. (2015). Trivial Compiler Equivalence: A Large Scale Empirical Study of a Simple, Fast and Effective Equivalent Mutant Detection Technique. 2015 IEEE/ACM 37th IEEE International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE), pp. 936-946.
rows.model_type: general software (C programs: 6 large open-source programs and 18 benchmark programs)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - applies mutation operators and uses compiler technology to discard equivalent and duplicated mutants, checked against hand-analysed equivalents.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - no stimulation protocols; equivalence screening is compiler-based rather than execution-based per the abstract.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no electrophysiology or dynamical-output features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - screens mutants; does not select a compact test or protocol battery.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - empirical study over program sets; no discovery/held-out split reported in the abstract.
rows.software: none (technique relies on existing compilers; no tool URL retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: TCE is a cheap static screen that catches only part of equivalent mutants. NeuroSem could add an analogous structural pre-screen, but its equivalence labels come from executing a finite neuron-model stimulation battery.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1109/icse.2015.103 (title, 4 authors incl. Le Traon, ICSE 2015 pp. 936-946); OpenAlex W4238681179 abstract.

rows.citation: Ammann P, Delamaro ME, Offutt J (2014). Establishing Theoretical Minimal Sets of Mutants. 2014 IEEE Seventh International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST), pp. 21-30.
rows.model_type: general software (mutation analysis theory, evaluated on a widely-used benchmark)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - studies mutant sets and their redundancy; shows how to minimise a mutant set with respect to a given test set.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - conventional software test cases; no stimulation protocols.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - minimises the mutant set relative to tests (dual of choosing tests to cover mutants); no protocol-battery selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - abstract reports evaluation on one benchmark; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Warns that redundant mutants inflate mutation scores. NeuroSem's detection matrix could report subsumption-aware rates alongside raw ones; its own contribution is protocol selection for neuron models, not mutant-set minimisation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1109/icst.2014.13 (title, 3 authors, ICST 2014 pp. 21-30); OpenAlex W2008479535 abstract.

rows.citation: Papadakis M, Kintis M, Zhang J, et al. (2019). Mutation Testing Advances: An Analysis and Survey. Advances in Computers (Elsevier), pp. 275-378.
rows.model_type: general software testing (survey of mutation testing research)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - surveys a decade of advances on fundamental mutation-testing problems and best practice for mutation in empirical studies.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - software testing context; abstract mentions no stimulation protocols.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear - abstract mentions mutation guiding test generation; coverage of test-suite selection not verified from the full chapter.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - literature survey without its own held-out empirical evaluation.
rows.ai_transformations: no - abstract does not mention AI-generated or AI-assisted transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A methodological handbook for using mutation in empirical studies. NeuroSem applies such practice to NeuroML neuron models with stimulation batteries, calibrated feature tolerances and held-out models and mutation families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1016/bs.adcom.2018.03.015 (title, Advances in Computers, pp. 275-378, 2019, book-chapter, no authors); authors from ORBilu hdl 10993/31612 citation metadata, cross-checked with OpenAlex W2725449579 and Semantic Scholar; abstract from Semantic Scholar Graph API.

rows.citation: Tian Z, Shu H, Wang D, et al. (2024). Large Language Models for Equivalent Mutant Detection: How Far Are We? Proceedings of the 33rd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis (ISSTA 2024), pp. 1733-1745.
rows.model_type: general software (3,302 method-level Java mutant pairs)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - classifies existing Java mutant pairs as equivalent or not, comparing LLM strategies with prior equivalent-mutant detection techniques.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - no stimulation protocols; equivalence judged from code.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no electrophysiology; metrics are classification scores and time overhead.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of a test or protocol battery.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract cites generalisation to unseen mutants as a motivation; train/test split details not verified from full text.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - LLMs act as equivalence classifiers of mutants, not as authors of code or model transformations.
rows.software: EMD replication package, https://github.com/tianzhaotju/EMD (GitHub API: no license detected)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses LLMs as static equivalence oracles on Java. NeuroSem labels equivalence by executing neuron models under a stimulation battery, and studies AI agents as transformation authors; LLM pre-screening would still need empirical confirmation.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abs page 2408.01760 (authors, date, abstract, ISSTA comment); Crossref /works/10.1145/3650212.3680395 (published version, pp. 1733-1745); OpenAlex W4402442864; GitHub REST API repos/tianzhaotju/EMD.

rows.citation: Inozemtseva L, Holmes R (2014). Coverage is not strongly correlated with test suite effectiveness. Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE 2014), pp. 435-445.
rows.model_type: general software (five large Java systems; generated unit test suites)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - mutation testing measures fault-detection effectiveness of 31,000 generated suites.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - software unit test suites; no stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - measures statement, decision and modified-condition coverage and mutation-based effectiveness.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - studies correlations between size, coverage and effectiveness; no optimised suite selection reported in the abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - correlational study across five systems; no discovery/held-out split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows suite size confounds effectiveness comparisons, supporting NeuroSem's count- and runtime-matched random baselines. NeuroSem instead tests whether a greedily selected protocol battery beats such baselines on held-out neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1145/2568225.2568271 (title, 2 authors, ICSE '14 pp. 435-445); full abstract from ACM DL landing page; OpenAlex W2106072155.
